$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. DeviceOperation per FB-RAT-DEV-002 (device object model), operationalizing the 7-step flash contract (FB-RAT-DEV-004/005/006/007) and the FB-RAT-DEV-001 Device Broker's exclusive-lock + explicit-destructive-authority requirements. Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<DeviceOperation> (see schemas/common/envelope.schema.json). `operationId` is this object's own FB-RAT-COM-002 stable ID.
title: DeviceOperation
description: One device-broker-arbitrated operation (flash, erase, read-back verify, self-test, a serial session, or a debug session): preconditions, explicit destructive authority, the firmware artifact (when applicable), protocol progress, verification, rollback, and a terminal receipt. See docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §4 for the full 7-step flash-contract table this schema structurally enforces the checkable half of.

operationId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this operation (FB-RAT-COM-002).

connectionId.description: References DeviceConnection.connectionId (schemas/devices/connection.schema.json) — the connection this operation runs over.

operationKind.description: FB-RAT-DEV-001: the operation classes the Device Broker arbitrates (serial, flash, debug, plus the read-back-verify and self-test steps the flash contract itself requires, plus a standalone erase). FLASH and ERASE are the destructive classes the explicit-authority gate (§authority) applies to most directly.

artifactId.description: References FirmwareArtifact.firmwareArtifactId (schemas/devices/firmware-artifact.schema.json) — required non-null when operationKind is FLASH (see the if/then below), null for every other operationKind (ERASE writes no image; READ_BACK_VERIFY/SELF_TEST/SERIAL_SESSION/DEBUG_SESSION do not carry an image at all).

receipt.description: Non-null only once `state` has reached a terminal value (SUCCEEDED, FAILED_SAFE, FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE, TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN, CANCELLED) — flash contract step 7. Null while the operation is still PENDING_PRECONDITIONS/AUTHORIZED/IN_PROGRESS/VERIFYING.

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

allOf.$comment: A FLASH operation MUST reference the firmware image it is writing.

FB-RAT-DEV-005: SUCCEEDED requires verification.state=VERIFIED — flash contract step 6 gates step 7's last-known-good update. There is no 'succeeded unverified' terminal state for DeviceOperation, unlike ExecutionReceipt — an unverified completion is FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE or TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN, never a silent SUCCEEDED.

Flash contract step 4: a destructive (FLASH/ERASE) operation that has progressed past preconditions into IN_PROGRESS or beyond MUST carry explicit destructive authorization — it cannot have reached the erase/write stage any other way.

FB-RAT-DEV-007 (wrong-board block, and preconditions failures generally): FAILED_SAFE means the operation was blocked BEFORE any destructive action — its receipt (if present) MUST record zero side effects, never a generic/ambiguous failure that leaves open whether erase started.

FB-RAT-DEV-006: disconnect after erase but before verification MUST resolve to FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE (never a generic failure) and MUST record at least one side effect — see fixtures/devices/adversarial/disconnect-mid-flash.adversarial.json.
FB-RAT-DEV-006's other permitted outcome for a disconnect whose destructive-progress point cannot even be established: a receipt MUST still exist, recording what is known.

identityConfidenceAtLeast.description: Flash contract step 1/3: the minimum DeviceIdentity.confidence.level this operation requires before it may proceed past PENDING_PRECONDITIONS. A destructive operationKind (FLASH/ERASE) SHOULD require at least PROBABLE; requiring only UNCERTAIN or UNKNOWN for a destructive operation is a policy choice this schema permits representing but does not itself forbid — see docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §4 for the provider-gate obligation this implies.

usbPermissionGranted.description: Flash contract step 2: mirrors DeviceConnection.usbPermissionGranted at the time this operation was created — duplicated here (rather than only read live from the connection) so a completed operation's own historical record is self-contained.

boardFirmwareCompatibilityChecked.description: Flash contract step 3: whether the DeviceIdentity.board vs FirmwareArtifact.boardCompatibility check (FB-RAT-DEV-007 wrong-board block) has been run. A destructive operationKind MUST NOT reach AUTHORIZED with this false — see docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §4.

powerWiringAssumptionsAcknowledged.description: Flash contract step 3: whether power/wiring assumptions (e.g. 'board is USB-powered, no external supply required', 'ISP wiring confirmed by user') have been surfaced and acknowledged. Free-form by design — the exact assumptions vary per board/protocol family and are not enumerated in this contract.

exclusiveLockId.description: FB-RAT-DEV-001: references the DeviceLock.lockId (schemas/devices/connection.schema.json) the Device Broker granted for this operation. Non-blank — a DeviceOperation cannot be modeled without holding the broker's exclusive lock, mirroring FB-RAT-COM-012 'no contract bypass' the same way ExecutionRequest.authorityGrant does in the execution domain.

destructiveActionExplicitlyAuthorized.description: Flash contract step 4: explicit, non-implicit authorization for a destructive action (erase/write), separate from merely holding the lock. A user or agent can hold the exclusive lock (e.g. to run a non-destructive SELF_TEST) without this being true; FLASH/ERASE operations require it true before progressing past AUTHORIZED (see the top-level if/then).

authorizedAtUtc.description: Null while state=PENDING_PRECONDITIONS (authorization not yet granted).

family.description: Which of the nine FB-RAT-DEV-010 families this operation's wire protocol uses. Duplicated locally from schemas/devices/device-identity.schema.json's $defs/UsbFamily per this repo's shared-sub-shape convention (docs/ratified/COMMON_CONVENTIONS.md §5).

progressPercent.description: Flash contract step 5: bootloader/transfer progress. Null before IN_PROGRESS begins, or for a protocol/transport that cannot report granular progress (some report only start/done).

sideEffectsPossible.description: Flash contract step 5's 'recorded possible side effects': flips true the moment a destructive transfer (erase/write) actually begins, independent of whether the operation ultimately succeeds — this is the field a disconnect handler reads to decide between FAILED_SAFE (still false — nothing destructive started yet) and FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE/TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN (true — something may have happened).

DeviceOperationState.description: Non-terminal: PENDING_PRECONDITIONS, AUTHORIZED, IN_PROGRESS, VERIFYING. Terminal: SUCCEEDED, FAILED_SAFE, FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE, TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN, CANCELLED. See docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §4 for the full from-state/trigger/to-state table mapping this directly onto the 7-step flash contract; FAILED_SAFE is reached only from PENDING_PRECONDITIONS (FB-RAT-DEV-007 — wrong-board and other precondition failures happen strictly before erase), never from IN_PROGRESS or VERIFYING.

method.description: Flash contract step 6's four verification methods.

possible.description: Whether this operation has a defined rollback path. Honest default for FLASH/ERASE on many embedded targets is `false` — once erase has begun, the prior firmware is generally gone unless a full prior-image backup exists as a FirmwareArtifact to re-flash from, which is not the same as an in-protocol rollback.

steps.description: MUST be non-empty when possible=true, and MUST be empty when possible=false (mirrors schemas/common/migration-plan.schema.json's RollbackPlan pattern) — a plan MUST NOT claim rollback steps it does not actually support.

exitState.description: The terminal subset of DeviceOperationState — mirrors the outer `state` at the instant this receipt was written.

sideEffects.description: Flash contract steps 5-7: real-world effects this operation is known (or believed) to have caused. Required non-empty when exitState=FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE (see the top-level if/then).

errorEnvelope.description: Reused as-is from schemas/common/error.schema.json (not redefined here). Non-null on any failed/uncertain exitState; null for SUCCEEDED.

snapshotAfterId.description: References the DeviceSnapshot.snapshotId (schemas/devices/snapshot.schema.json) taken immediately after this operation, when one was taken. This is the snapshot whose lastKnownGood field is expected to flip true for a SUCCEEDED+VERIFIED flash (FB-RAT-DEV-005).
